capabilities: Sync a shared vault in real time across desktop and mobile through a self-hosted server
Merge non-overlapping edits automatically and keep both versions as conflict copies
Track who wrote each change in an Activity panel and restore past note versions
Invite and approve members with a one-time invitation and a 6-digit voice handshake
Run background AI agents as vault members with task notes (optional)
extras: No end-to-end encryption: the server stores the vault in plaintext, so whoever controls the server machine can read everything; the README includes a security model and privacy disclosures. Syncs only an .obsidian/ appearance allowlist, never plugins, and only attachments up to 25 MB (PNG, JPG, GIF, WebP, SVG, PDF).
problem: Obsidian's own Sync is a hosted service, and small groups who want to share one vault on hardware they control have no self-hosted option with per-author history and conflict handling.

relations.evidence: Set up Tailscale. Make a free account, turn on MagicDNS and HTTPS certificates in its admin console
With a local Ollama nothing leaves.
run Claude, MCP or another local agent in that vault, its edits land in the same history

requires.name: Self-hosted Havemind server (your own hardware, Docker install script or manual build)
Model provider API key for AI agents (or local Ollama)

summary: Self-hosted real-time vault sync for two or three people, with authorship tracking, conflict copies, per-note history and optional AI agents as members.
